(bot-b relay worker writes no job status; its wrangler config needs no var.)

investigation.confirmed_root_cause: CONFIRMED via 19/19 on-disk jobs + live releases + actual cleanup run 34469909937 log (2026-09-10T11:10Z, now=1789038644, ttl=43200). NO expires_at_epoch mutation/renewal exists: the only writers are bot/src/jobs.js::newStatus (create) and pipeline/status.py (initial write + missing-field backfill); git history of manual-1787970449255/status.json shows only creation-time 12h writes plus bot mergeStatus updates that (post-fix-1) never rewrite an existing expires_at_epoch (pin: merge-never-rewrites-expiry test). Stored expires_at_epoch values are correctly computed (created+43200) and ARE in the past for the stuck jobs — expiry computation is fine. The mechanism is a SEMANTIC DEADLOCK in the bug-66 guard (series_is_complete in pipeline/cleanup/expired.py): a series is 'complete' only when every on-disk part is terminal AND at least one part is marked is_final=true. The bot never auto-queues a next part — the operator must press 'Start next part' — and only the FINAL part ever carries is_final=true. Every job in this repo has series.enabled=true (even one-off 'manual-' jobs get a series_id), so ANY abandoned/non-finalized series has zero is_final parts and is classified INCOMPLETE FOREVER, and the guard protects its expired parts on every hourly run indefinitely (exact log lines: 'PROTECT job=manual-1788609489376 — series series-1788609521896 incomplete'). 8 distinct single/two-part series with all parts terminal, expires_at_epoch 2-11 days in the past, are kept solely by this guard; 2 jobs (manual-1787970449255, series-1787970477573-p2) are metadata-only folders whose releases were already destroyed by the pre-bug-66 run 1d6ad63 and restored by recovery 0e2f9d7 — they are stuck for the same guard reason. The younger series (1788993144175, 1789002249271) are NOT stuck: their stored expires_at_epoch were still in the future at the examined run (old 12h math; fix #1 makes new jobs 48h) or have a genuinely non-terminal sibling (awaiting_plan). Root cause is therefore NOT a TTL-duration problem (that was fix #1) and NOT an expiry-computation bug — it is that the protective guard has no time-based exit: a series abandoned before its final part can never become complete, so its parts can never expire.

fix_2_stuck_jobs.approach: Add a time-based exit to the zero-final deadlock WITHOUT weakening in-flight protection: series_is_complete gains a finalization-grace rule — when no part is marked is_final, the series is complete iff EVERY on-disk part is terminal AND every part's expires_at_epoch is in the past (unknown/missing expiry = protected, safe). A series whose newest part is still within its TTL (e.g. scheduled publishing still pending, next part plausibly coming) stays protected exactly as today; a series with a non-terminal sibling stays protected exactly as today (bug-49). With fix #1's 48h TTL, an abandoned series' parts are reaped 48h after the LAST part was created instead of never. Also: bot/src/jobs.js mergeStatus missing-expiry backfill switches from hardcoded DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS to configuredJobTtlSeconds(env) (consistency with fix #1; backfill never fires for real jobs, defensive only). Existing status.json files are NOT edited: no data correction is needed — the stored expires_at_epoch values are correct; the fix is in the DECISION logic, and the next hourly sweep (post-deploy) naturally reaps the confirmed-abandoned expired series.
